dataset_family: Literature synthesis with no primary cohort: 126 published observational studies (PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, Web of Science, searched to 15 January 2021; PROSPERO CRD42020175096). The included-study list is in Supplementary file 3, which is not in the extract.
method_family: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis (Cohen's d SMD and ratio of means), with meta-regression, subgroup analyses and publication-bias tests. Narrative synthesis where fewer than 2 homogeneous studies.
what_it_shows:
Ge, Xu, ... Tan, Zhao and Yu 2021, Ageing Research Reviews.
- Pooled OCT data show thinner pRNFL (SMD -0.324), total macula (-0.302), mRNFL, mGCIPL, mGCC and subfoveal choroid (-0.462) in clinically defined MCI than in controls. Retinal vessel complexity is also lower in MCI (k=4 fundus-camera studies plus OCTA). OCTA microvascular densities showed no significant MCI difference.
- The three MCI-vs-CN diagnostic-accuracy studies it found reported AUCs of 0.47 to 0.72.
- A large population-based study found no MCI-control difference in inner retina or total macular thickness. All four population-based fundus-camera vascular cohorts were negative.
- The authors conclude that retinal markers 'could not be translated into clinical practice yet' and 'could not be used at the individual level yet'.
- It covers retina only, not eye movements.
why:
PDF identity confirmed. The title, the 11 authors, Ageing Research Reviews 69 (2021) 101361 and DOI 10.1016/j.arr.2021.101361 match the block. I read the whole extract, including Table 1 and its limitation key, up to the References.

STATED FORM, no. This is a synthesis. Under the round-21 rule a review or meta-analysis supports only a statement about syntheses. The Table A1 record is a convergence claim that has to be carried by independent primary studies' own data. P-830 has no participants of its own and pools other studies, so it cannot be a supporter of this convergence. Round 20 applied the same rule to P-105. The finder itself said it cannot raise the count of independent primary cohorts.

Its content would also only partly match even if syntheses counted:
(a) Retinal thinning in MCI is a small effect (SMDs -0.19 to -0.60) with 'moderate to high heterogeneity' (p.3).
(b) MCI discrimination in the three accuracy studies was AUC 0.47-0.72, and those studies were case-control designs likely to overestimate it (p.3).
(c) The population-based evidence, the best available test of scalability, was null for MCI thickness (Ito 2020) and for all four vascular cohorts (pp.3, 5). Table 1 attaches 'c, poor applicability due to predominantly clinical-based' and 'a, lack of AD specificity' to almost every MCI cell.
(d) Eye movements are not covered.

NARROWED FORM, no. The narrowed wording describes specific single-centre primary cohorts. A pooled synthesis neither is one nor demonstrates one.

INDEPENDENCE. The search closed on 15 January 2021. P-952 was received 11 August 2021 and published 6 November 2021 (checked in its PDF). P-966 is from 2022 and P-5 from 2023. None of the three supporters can be among the 126 included studies. P-105 is a 2025 review. Among the candidates, P-224 (2023), P-1152 (2025) and P-255 (2026) all postdate the search, so none of them can be among the included studies either. No shared authors with any supporter or candidate. Not a preprint: a peer-reviewed article in Ageing Research Reviews.

quotes.quote: Compared with healthy controls, patients with MCI also had lower thickness of pRNFL (SMD = -0.324, p < 0.001), total macular (SMD = -0.302, p < 0.001), and subfoveal choroid (SMD = -0.462, p = 0.020).
PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, and Web of Science were systematically searched without language and date restrictions by two independent authors till January 15, 2021.
Most studies investigated the diagnostic value of retinal biomarkers, whereas only seven studies were longitudinal and assessed the risk or prognostic value.

In conflict with the meta-analysis of small sample studies, a large population-based study did not detect any difference between MCI and controls regarding the inner retina and TMT (Ito et al., 2020). For the diagnostic performance, AUC was reported in six studies that distinguishing clinically-defined AD with CN (from 0.48 to 0.97), and three studies distinguishing clinically-defined MCI with CN (from 0.47 to 0.72).

There were four large sample population-based studies with fundus camera imaging exploring vascular biomarkers in AD or MCI, two cross-sectional (Baker et al., 2007; Lee et al., 2019) and two longitudinal (de Jong et al., 2011; Deal et al., 2019). None of them reported positive findings.
Therefore, the retinal markers could not be translated into clinical practice yet.
Although retinal biomarkers could not be used at the individual level yet, the fast innovation of technologies enables researchers to investigate retinal features more readily than ever before.

‡ Limitation: a, lack of AD specificity; b, high heterogeneity (I2 > 50 % in meta-analysis or inconsistent results in systematic review); c, poor applicability due to predominantly clinical-based; d, insufficient number of studies (no meta- analysis or less than five studies pooled in meta-analysis)
